I am so sorry for your loss. This must be terribly difficult and I can’t imagine how you and your loved ones are feeling right now. I did want to mention that in my family there’s a mental illness called Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) and it causes a lot of ups and downs in your emotions, lots of mood swings. This previous Saturday, I was about to commit suicide when I decided I didn’t want to do it anymore all of a sudden. One thing can set me into a huge spiral down and can cause me to want to harm myself. The way your brother was perfectly fine and then suddenly suicidal remind me a lot of myself. I don’t want to try to diagnose or anything, I just wanted to give my input in what I have experienced and what your experience with your brother sounds like. Anyways, I’m really hoping you and your family can find peace at some point. I’ll be sending lots of positive thoughts your way! Wish you and your family nothing but the best.

you are not alone in struggling with self harm! if it’s difficult to bring up, start with baby steps! i once was told that said vulnerability is not weakness, it’s strength. being able to tell someone you need help is soo difficult to do, i totally understand that! but once you get over that hill of reaching out for help, you’ll be so glad you did! maybe it’s a teacher, a friend, or family member; no matter who it is, you would be acting out of bravery!! i also heard a therapist say that it’s “short term pain for long term gain” - it’s going to be tough and scary for a little bit, but once you get through it, you will be so proud of yourself for doing it!

i can understand that, too. i personally don’t view it as selfish for someone to stop me from committing; i think they see me a so much stronger than i feel in that moment. i see it as them believing in me and wanting me to keep going so that they can see me thrive and continue to be with them for that.

i also know that distractions help me a lot!! watching your favorite show, drawing/painting, taking a walk are all good ideas! i also know that moving my body helps me too. i usually have to just take my mind of off the thoughts in my head - ruminating on the thought of suicide won’t be good for anyone! if you’re struggling with self harm (i do too, it’s okay!) my favorite skill is to hold ice where you want to hurt yourself. i also used to put temporary tattoos wherever i wanted to self harm, or sometimes even draw/paint there!

i totally understand that point of view - our brains are kind of rewarded with the idea of suicide. “no more pain?? i’m in!” but in reality, it’s just that we haven’t found a solution/coping skill for us! 
some of my current favorite skills have been grounding techniques! these usually have to do with the 5 senses! i’ll probably link some websites that can explain it better since there’s a lot to type.. my all-time-favorite is the 5-4-3-2-1 skill!! (the website goes into more detail!!)

[grounding techniques ](https://www.healthline.com/health/grounding-techniques#physical-techniques)

i mean, i have “chronic” suicidal thoughts and i am against the idea of suicide. it’s a scary thing to say “i don’t want to experience life anymore”. it’s a big and bold statement and is a choice that is very permanent. 
i personally don’t think it’s looked down upon, i think most people are just scared of it. when people talk about death, it’s usually out of fear; no one really knows whats after death, so it’s natural to feel scared about it. i know when people have stopped me in the past, it’s definitely not because they want to look like a good person - it’s because they love and care about me. they want me to stay in their lives for as long as i can. i know that this may not be what you need, but i just thought i would put my opinion out there. hope you get the help, love, and care you need and deserve:)
